items.readable_text:
Content:
Suppose that the sequence [MATH: a_n] is defined as
[MATH: a_n = 3\left(\dfrac 1 2\right)^n, \qquad n\geq 1.]
This is a geometric sequence with common ratio [MATH: r = \dfrac12.] What is the behavior of this sequence as [MATH: n\to\infty?]

Content:
Let's start by calculating the first few terms of the sequence:

Content:
[MATH: a_1 = \dfrac32, \qquad a_2 = \dfrac34, \qquad a_3 = \dfrac38, \qquad a_4 = \dfrac{3}{16}, \qquad \ldots\,.]

Content:
Plotting the few terms of the sequence, we get a graph like the one below:

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/67a6cc016cc67914bfcdb28a0d701876]

Content:
From the diagram, it appears that [MATH: a_n\to 0] as [MATH: n\to\infty.] This is indeed true.

Content:
Because [MATH: a_n] approaches zero as [MATH: n\to \infty,] we say that the sequence is convergent and that it converges to [MATH: 0.] We also say that the limit of the sequence is [MATH: 0.]

Content:
The sequence is convergent because [MATH: |r| < 1,] which causes the terms of the sequence to decrease to zero as [MATH: n] increases.

Let's start by calculating the first few terms of the sequence:

Content:
[MATH: b_1 = 2, \qquad b_2 = 4, \qquad b_3 = 8, \qquad b_4 = 16, \qquad \ldots\,.]

Plotting the few terms of the sequence, we get a graph like the one below:

Content:
Because [MATH: b_n] grows without bound as [MATH: n\to \infty,] we say that the sequence is divergent. The sequence is divergent because [MATH: |r| > 1,] which causes the terms of the sequence to increase as [MATH: n] increases.

items.title: Determining Whether a Geometric Sequence Converges

sections.normalized_html:
Consider the following geometric sequence: [MATH: 6, \quad -2, \quad \dfrac{2}{3}, \quad -\dfrac{2}{9}, \quad \ldots]

Determine whether the sequence is convergent or divergent. If it converges, find the limit.
sections.readable_text:
Consider the following geometric sequence:
[MATH: 6, \quad -2, \quad \dfrac{2}{3}, \quad -\dfrac{2}{9}, \quad \ldots]

Determine whether the sequence is convergent or divergent. If it converges, find the limit.

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
Suppose we have a geometric sequence with the first term [MATH: a_1] and common ratio [MATH: r.] Then, we have the following convergence properties:

  • if [MATH: |r| < 1,] the sequence is convergent and converges to [MATH: 0]

  • if [MATH: |r| > 1,] the sequence is divergent

Moreover, we have the following edge cases:

  • if [MATH: r=1,] the sequence is convergent and converges to [MATH: a_1]

  • if [MATH: r = -1,] the sequence is divergent

The given sequence is a geometric sequence with the common ratio

[MATH: r=\dfrac{a_2}{a_1}=\dfrac{(-2)}{6}= -\dfrac{1}{3}.]

Since [MATH: |r| = \dfrac{1}{3} < 1,] the sequence converges to [MATH: 0.]

- if [MATH: r = -1,] the sequence is divergent
